issues.body: The previous finding is unresolved. Section 8.1 again says `record_partition_reservation`, `record_partition_defer`, and `assemble-census` already print everything needed, that no new code is required, and that one pass over the same log can classify global holders as `__global__`-only versus `__global__` plus narrow atoms. The cited reservation census describes candidate rows, not busy occupancy rows; the defer census splits candidate deferrals by reason; and the existing occupancy census does not preserve each holder's reserved-set shape jointly with cause. The fact that `busy_packages_of_pulls` has `cause` and the reserved set in memory at decision time does not put them into historical logs. Thus old runs cannot determine whether a global-reserving tick was narrow-free or reconstruct the requested holder-shape split.
issues.fix_hint: State explicitly that historical logs cannot answer these occupancy questions. Specify and add, before any observation window, a zero-sealed emitted occupancy census that records at least global-holder reserved-set shape (`global-only` versus `global-plus-narrow`) and its joint breakdown by cause, plus whether any non-exempt busy occupant reserves a narrow atom. Then require a fresh observation window. Alternatively, cite an existing emitted artifact and exact fields that actually preserve this joint occupancy evidence; do not cite candidate-row aggregates or in-memory values as retrospective evidence.
issues.title: Section 8.1 still claims unavailable occupancy evidence exists in old logs

verdict.summary: The prior round's major evidence-path defect remains materially unchanged. Section 8.1 still says the required holder-shape and narrow-occupant measurements are already printed and recoverable from existing run logs, but the cited emissions do not preserve those occupancy attributes. The document correctly notes that `busy_packages_of_pulls` has each row's cause and reserved set in memory; that does not make those fields available retrospectively. Candidate-row `by_reservation` data cannot establish whether busy occupants reserve narrow atoms, and cause-only occupancy aggregates cannot recover the joint `(cause, reserved-set shape)` split. Because this measurement is the prescribed prerequisite for an overrule and determines whether reading (B)'s release population exists, the record is not yet operationally complete.
